players.product: Hyperscale AI data-center campus with behind-the-meter power (Project Matador, Texas): powered land, powered shell and turnkey data centers leased to AI compute tenants (first tenant TensorWave, 222 MW initial phase)

quarterly_data.signal: Supplier Siemens Energy: Fermi's 10-Q states that as of June 30, 2026 it had purchase commitments of approximately $142.6 million under executed contracts with Siemens Energy for the supply of three SGT6-5000F and six SGT-800 gas turbine generator units for Project Matador, payable on contract milestones; the unconditional purchase obligations for these long-lead-time equipment purchases fall due $38,430 thousand in 2026, $71,279 thousand in 2027 and $32,940 thousand in 2028. Fermi had already made payments to Siemens Energy of $201.6 million under the F-Class equipment purchase agreement, and the six SGT-800 units are bought under an equipment supply agreement originally entered into in October 2025. Under a Rated Capacity Agreement, additional contingent consideration for the three SGT6-5000F turbines, Fermi will pay Siemens up to $2 million per turbine per calendar quarter based on each turbine's operating reliability (not less than $80 thousand per turbine per quarter) for ten years from provisional acceptance, subject to a maximum of approximately $240.0 million undiscounted.
quarterly_data.figure: Siemens Energy purchase commitments approximately $142.6 million (three SGT6-5000F + six SGT-800), as of June 30, 2026; $201.6 million paid under the F-Class agreement; Rated Capacity Agreement up to approximately $240.0 million over ten years

quarterly_data.signal: Fermi's 10-Q capital plan for Project Matador: incremental capex to complete Phase 0 and Phase 1 could exceed $3 billion, of which approximately $2 billion is expected in the next twelve months, subject to the TensorWave Lease conditions and tenant deployment timelines; total capital needs across all phases could range from approximately $70 billion to $90 billion, depending on EPC costs still being negotiated, power-equipment configuration (largely complete for Phase 1), tax-credit qualification of the nuclear and solar parts, and long-term forecasting uncertainty. As of June 30, 2026 Fermi had not generated any revenues.
quarterly_data.figure: Phase 0 + Phase 1 capex could exceed $3 billion (approximately $2 billion in the next twelve months); all phases approximately $70 billion to $90 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Fermi's 10-Q long-range power plan: a roadmap to deploy four Westinghouse reactors, with one Westinghouse reactor unit commissioned in each of 2033, 2034, 2035 and 2036, alongside a multi-phase gas plan using GE 6B, Siemens SGT-800 and Siemens SGT6-5000F frame turbines plus TM2500 mobile aeroderivative units, commissioned first in simple cycle and later converted to combined cycle with heat recovery steam generators and steam turbines.
quarterly_data.figure: four Westinghouse reactors, one each in 2033, 2034, 2035 and 2036

quarterly_data.signal: Fermi's 10-Q on tenants and the Hillcore deal: Fermi entered into the TensorWave Lease on August 9, 2026, but its effectiveness remains subject to customary closing conditions including Board approvals and project-level financing; other than the TensorWave Lease, Fermi has not entered into definitive agreements with any other tenants. Under the Hillcore Framework Agreement (August 11, 2026) Hillcore would finance, build, own and operate up to approximately 2.6 GW of generation at Project Matador, including approximately 100 MW of solar and battery storage, with an initial block of approximately 360 MW not conditioned on tenant power purchase arrangements; Fermi would buy capacity under end-user PPAs on a take-or-pay basis equal to at least 50% of all tenants' aggregate power requirements, at a fixed capacity charge passed through to tenants, with gas costs passed through. The agreement has a three-year initial term and three-year exclusivity, and definitive documentation is still to be negotiated within 90 days.
quarterly_data.figure: Hillcore up to approximately 2.6 GW (approximately 100 MW solar and battery storage; initial block approximately 360 MW); take-or-pay at least 50% of tenant power requirements; no definitive tenant other than TensorWave
